Glogg Mulled Wine

Served at: Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil)

Serves 8-10Prep 10 minCook 20-30 min

Glogg, the aromatic and warming Scandinavian mulled wine, is a beloved tradition during the winter holidays. It is especially cherished during Lussinatta (St. Lucia's Vigil), where its comforting spices and sweet warmth bring cheer to the long, dark nights, symbolizing light and hospitality.

Ingredients

  • 2 (750 ml) bottles dry red wine (such as Merlot or Cabernet Sauvignon)
  • 1 cup (240 ml) port wine or brandy (optional, for a stronger Glogg)
  • 1/2 cup (100 g) granulated sugar, or to taste
  • 10-12 whole cloves
  • 8-10 green cardamom pods, lightly crushed
  • 4-5 cinnamon sticks
  • 1 (2-inch / 5 cm) piece fresh ginger, peeled and thinly sliced
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) blanched almonds
  • 1/2 cup (60 g) golden raisins
  • Orange peel from 1 orange (use a vegetable peeler to get strips without pith)

Method

  1. Combine the red wine, port or brandy (if using), sugar, cloves, crushed cardamom pods, cinnamon sticks, ginger slices, and orange peel in a large non-reactive pot or Dutch oven.
  2. Heat the mixture over medium-low heat, stirring occasionally, until the sugar has dissolved.
  3. Continue to heat gently, ensuring the Glogg does not boil. Boiling will cause the alcohol to evaporate and can alter the flavor.
  4. Let the Glogg simmer gently for at least 20-30 minutes to allow the flavors to meld and deepen. The longer it simmers (without boiling), the more pronounced the spice flavors will become.
  5. Taste and adjust sweetness if desired, adding more sugar a tablespoon at a time until it reaches your preference.
  6. Just before serving, stir in the blanched almonds and golden raisins.
  7. Serve warm in mugs or heatproof glasses, ensuring each serving gets some almonds and raisins from the bottom of the pot.

Tips

  • For an extra festive touch, garnish each mug with a fresh orange slice or a star anise pod.
  • You can prepare the Glogg a day in advance; store it in the refrigerator and gently reheat before serving. The flavors often improve overnight.
  • If you prefer a non-alcoholic version, substitute the red wine with cranberry juice or blackcurrant juice and omit the port/brandy.
